shipped_rows.title_o: Evaluating the Association between Keratoconus and Reported Genetic Loci in a Han Chinese Population

blind_target.authors: Wang YM, Ma L, Lu SY, Chan TCY, Yam JCS, Tang SM, et al.
blind_target.title: Analysis of multiple genetic loci reveals MPDZ-NF1B rs1324183 as a putative genetic marker for keratoconus.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
In recently years, Wang YM and Hao XD et al. both analyzed the association of SNP locus with keratoconus in Chinese population, and revealed that the rs1324183 (
MPDZ-NF1B
), which located between the
MPDZ
and
NF1B
genes, is a putative genetic marker for monitoring the progression of keratoconus and should be further investigated in other different Chinese populations [
23
,
24
]. Thence, in this study, we collected a total of 114 KC patients who live in northwestern of China for the first time and further confirmed the association between the rs1324183 (
MPDZ-NF1B
) and KC, providing a clear basis for early clinical diagnosis in Chinese population.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
Notably, many studies have reported that the SNP rs1324183 (
MPDZ-NFIB
) is a genetic marker highly correlated with KC cases [
23
,
24
,
30
,
31
,
33
], and in our population, we have also further confirmed that the genotype AA of rs1324183 confers a higher risk for KC (Table
2
).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly confirm the shared SNP–KC association and risk genotype in their independent Chinese sample.

luna_triage.reason: The source says it performed a replication study of rs1324183 in an independent Chinese population and confirms that association; citation [24] identifies Wang et al. (2018) as a specific prior report of that locus. Shipped row 790 is Hao et al. (2015), a distinct original report, not an alternate citation for Wang et al. (2018).
